questions.stem: What are scientists planning to do?
options: A) Land a space vehicle on the moon in 2019.
B) Design a new generation of mobile phones.
C) Set up a mobile phone network on the moon.
D) Gather data from the moon with a tiny device.

explain.定位:
If successful, the tiny device will provide the moon with its first-ever mobile phone network.
如果成功，这个微型装置将为月球提供它有史以来第一个移动电话网络。
explain.信号:
核心任务陈述句。这句把整个任务的目标一句话点明：provide the moon with its first-
ever mobile phone network，是科学家此行要做的核心动作。新闻把 "要干什么" 直接平
铺直叙地说出来，没有转折，这种直陈核心任务的句子就是答案句。
explain.替换:
provide the moon with its first-ever mobile phone network ↔
Set up a mobile phone network on the moon
provide = set up
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到 to the moon in 2019，A 项 Land a space vehicle on the moon in 2019.
就盗用了 moon 和 2019 这两个原词，让人 "听到就想选"。但录音是说 2019 年送去 4G
网络任务，核心动作是 "建网络"，不是 "让飞行器着陆"，答非所问。
借用原文：deliver fourth generation or 4G mobile coverage to the moon in 2019
B) 原词陷阱
录音多次出现 mobile phone（手机），B 项 Design a new generation of mobile
phones. 借 mobile phone 这个原词，把任务说成 "设计新一代手机"。但录音说的是
4G/5G 是网络的 generation（代际），任务是建网络，不是设计手机这个硬件，属于偷
换。
借用原文：deliver fourth generation or 4G mobile coverage to the moon
D) 原词陷阱
录音里确有 A device that weighs less than one kilogram 和 streaming of video and
data，D 项 Gather data from the moon with a tiny device. 把 tiny device、data 两个
原词拼成 "用小装置收集数据"。但录音里小装置是用来 "提供网络" 的，data 是网络要传输
的内容，不是科学家此行的目的；任务核心仍是建网络，故 D 答非所问。
借用原文：high-definition streaming of video and data between the moon and Earth

questions.stem: Why did scientists choose to set up a 4G network in their mission?

explain.定位:
This is because fifth generation networks are still in testing and trial phases. This means that a
5G network may not yet be stable enough to work on the moon's surface.
这是因为第五代网络仍处于测试和试验阶段。这意味着 5G 网络可能还不够稳定，无法在月
球表面工作。
explain.信号:
because 因果信号。This is because 是明确的因果信号词，紧跟其后的就是 "为什么选 4G
不选 5G" 的原因；再加上 not yet be stable enough 一句把理由落到 "5G 还不够稳定"
上。听到 because 就锁这一段。
explain.替换:
a 5G network may not yet be stable enough to work on the moon's surface ↔ It is stable.
否定 5G 不稳 = 4G 稳
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
录音通篇没提网络 "耐用"（durable），只谈稳定与测试阶段。B 项 It is durable. 是凭 "好
东西应该耐用" 的常识硬填的，原文无据。
C) 未提及
"选便宜的方案" 是生活常识里最顺的理由，C 项 It is inexpensive. 极易凭想当然选中。但
录音给的理由只字未提价格，只说 5G 还不稳定，故 C 无中生有。
D) 与原文相反
D 项 It is sophisticated.（先进/复杂）方向反了：录音说更先进的 5G 还在测试、不够稳
定，所以才退而求其用更成熟的 4G。选 4G 恰恰不是因为它 "先进"，D 与原文逻辑相反。
借用原文：fifth generation networks are still in testing and trial phases
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Firefighters responded to a fire Wednesday night at an abandoned mall in Hayward. The fire was
reported at 9:26 p.m. at an old shopping centre on Mission Avenue near Saint Mary's church. Six fire
engines, two trucks and two chiefs responded to the scene. Crews had the fire under control in about 45
minutes and managed to contain the fire to its point of origin. There were some people inside the
building when the fire broke out, but there were no reports of any injuries. Fire investigators have
responded to the scene but have not yet determined the cause of the fire. Firefighters will remain on the
scene until later this morning to ensure that the fire doesn't start up again. The shopping mall had not
been in use since 2002. In 2014, City Hall developed a plan to knock down the building and replace it
with affordable housing. However, the plan was dropped due to lack of funds.
消防员周三晚上对Hayward一座废弃购物中心的火灾做出了响应。火灾于晚上9点26分在Mission
Avenue靠近Saint Mary's教堂的一座旧购物中心被报告。六辆消防车、两辆卡车和两名消防队长赶到现
场。消防人员在大约45分钟内控制住了火势,并成功将火势控制在起火点。火灾发生时建筑物内有一些人,
但没有人员伤亡的报告。火灾调查人员已赶到现场,但尚未确定起火原因。消防员将在现场留守至今天上午
晚些时候,以确保火势不会再次燃起。该购物中心自2002年以来一直未投入使用。2014年,市政厅制定了一
项计划,拟拆除该建筑并用经济适用房取而代之。然而,该计划因缺乏资金而被放弃。

questions.stem: What does the news item say about the fire?
options: A) It lasted more than six hours.
B) No injuries were yet reported.
C) Nobody was in the building when it broke out.
D) It had burned for 45 minutes by the time firefighters arrived.

explain.定位:
There were some people inside the building when the fire broke out, but there were no reports
of any injuries.
起火时楼里有一些人，但没有任何关于人员受伤的报告。
explain.信号:
转折 but 后是落点。这句的真意在转折词 but 之后：but there were no reports of any
injuries。前半 "有人在楼里" 是铺垫与干扰，转折后的"无人受伤"才是新闻要强调的事实，
正对应 B。
explain.替换:
there were no reports of any injuries ↔ No injuries were yet reported.
主被动换说法、意思不变
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
A 说火 lasted more than six hours，但录音是 Crews had the fire under control in
about 45 minutes——约 45 分钟就控制住，远不到六小时。A 用一个貌似具体的时长数字
来引诱"听到时间就选"，方向恰恰相反。
借用原文：Crews had the fire under control in about 45 minutes
C) 与原文相反
C 说 Nobody was in the building when it broke out.，可录音明说 There were some
people inside the building when the fire broke out——起火时"有"人。C 盗用了
"inside the building / broke out" 这串原词，却把"有人"反成"没人"，是把肯定听成否定
的典型反向陷阱。
借用原文：There were some people inside the building when the fire broke out
D) 原词陷阱
D 说 It had burned for 45 minutes by the time firefighters arrived.，确实把录音里的
45 分钟搬了过来，但录音的 Crews had the fire under control in about 45 minutes 说
的是"消防员用 45 分钟把火控制住"，不是"消防员到场前已烧了 45 分钟"。同一个数字被安
到了错误的事件上。
借用原文：Crews had the fire under control in about 45 minutes

questions.stem: What had City Hall planned to do?
options: A) Recruit and train more firefighters.
B) Pull down the deserted shopping mall.
C) Turn the shopping mall into an amusement park.
D) Find money to renovate the local neighborhood.

explain.定位:
In 2014, City Hall developed a plan to knock down the building and replace it with
affordable housing.
2014 年，市政厅制定了一项计划，要拆掉这座楼，换成保障性住房。
explain.信号:
信号词 developed a plan。锁定信号短语 developed a plan to knock down the
building，plan 后紧跟的动词 knock down（拆除）就是计划的核心动作，正对应 B。
explain.替换:
knock down the building ↔ Pull down the deserted shopping mall
knock down = pull down 同义
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
A 说 Recruit and train more firefighters.，借用了录音开头反复出现的 firefighters，但录
音从没提"招募培训消防员"，更不是市政厅的计划。它靠一个熟耳的原词把你往火灾前半段
拉，与"计划"这一问毫不相干。
借用原文：Firefighters responded to a fire Wednesday night
C) 未提及
C 说 Turn the shopping mall into an amusement park.，shopping mall 确是录音原
词，但"改建成游乐园"录音从未提及——计划是拆掉换成保障性住房，不是改游乐园。它用
对的对象配了个原文没有的动作。
借用原文：replace it with affordable housing
D) 张冠李戴
D 说 Find money to renovate the local neighborhood.，借用了录音结尾的 funds
（钱）。可录音说的是 the plan was dropped due to lack of funds——"因缺钱，计划被
放弃"，是计划告吹的原因，绝不是"市政厅的计划本身是去筹钱翻新社区"。同一个"钱"被安
到了错误的角色上。
借用原文：the plan was dropped due to lack of funds

questions.stem: What problem is Japan facing?

explain.定位:
Potato chips in Japan are being sold for 6 times their normal price. This is after the country's
main manufacturer stopped sales due to a potato shortage.
日本的薯片正以平常价格的 6 倍出售。这是因为该国主要的薯片厂商由于土豆短缺而停止了
销售。
explain.信号:
开篇点题加因果due to。新闻开篇即点出困境，且用因果信号 due to a potato shortage
把停售这一现象直接归到“土豆短缺”上。新闻第一句往往就是核心事件，加上 due to 这个
因果词，正是答案句的双重信号。
explain.替换:
a potato shortage ↔ Insufficient potato supply.
shortage等于supply不足
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
录音后文确实提到本地种植受天气影响，farming 类话题会被念到，A 项 Shrinking potato
farming. 借此制造“听到种植就想选”的诱惑；但新闻当下点明的问题是停售缺货，不是说种
植规模在长期萎缩，属答非所问。
借用原文：domestic produce could be seriously affected
B) 与原文相反
录音讲到日本限制进口土豆，import 一词被念到，B 项 Heavy reliance on import. 借这
个原词诱选；但原文是说日本“限制”进口、而非“严重依赖”进口，方向恰好相反，并非日本
面临的问题。
借用原文：Japanese laws limit the amount of imported potatoes
C) 张冠李戴
录音里 disease 确被反复念到，C 项 Widespread plant disease. 极易让人“听到 disease
就选”；但原文中 disease 是日本“限制进口的理由”，并不是日本当前面临的问题，且原文也
没说病害已 widespread（大面积蔓延），属张冠李戴。
借用原文：fear of disease is its main reason to block fresh imports

questions.stem: Why does Japan limit the import of potatoes?
options: A) It intends to keep its traditional diet.
B) It wants to expand its own farming.
C) It is afraid of the spread of disease.
D) It is worried about unfair competition.

explain.定位:
Japan says fear of disease is its main reason to block fresh imports.
日本表示，对病害的担忧是其封锁新鲜土豆进口的主要理由。
explain.信号:
reason直接给理由。这句里同时出现 main reason 和 block fresh imports，把“限制进口”
和它的理由直接绑在一句，是最典型的原因答案句信号——原文明说 reason 是什么，听到
reason 就锁这句。
explain.替换:
fear of disease ↔ It is afraid of the spread of disease.
fear名词转is afraid形容词
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
原文从未提到日本想保留传统饮食，A 项 It intends to keep its traditional diet. 属凭空添
加；它利用“薯片是日本人爱吃的零食”这种常识联想骗人，但录音里没有任何对应表述。
B) 原词陷阱
录音提到本地种植 domestic produce，farming 类话题被念到，B 项 It wants to expand
its own farming. 借此诱选；但原文是说本地产出可能受天气危害，从没说日本想“扩大”自
家种植，属答非所问的原词陷阱。
借用原文：domestic produce could be seriously affected
D) 未提及
D 项 It is worried about unfair competition. 的 unfair competition 是个听起来很合理的
“贸易保护”联想，但录音里压根没提竞争，限制进口的理由原文白纸黑字写的是怕病害，与
竞争无关。

questions.stem: What might affect Japanese domestic produce?

explain.定位:
But global warming has raised the possibility that domestic produce could be seriously
affected by rare weather events more often.
但是全球变暖加大了一种可能性：本地产出会更频繁地受到罕见天气事件的严重影响。
explain.信号:
转折But加篇末落点。这是新闻最后一句，且以转折词 But 起头，转折之后才是真正要强调
的言外之意；新闻篇末的转折句往往是全篇升华的落点，正是答案句信号。
explain.替换:
global warming has raised the possibility that domestic produce could be seriously affected ↔
Global warming.
施动者即影响因素
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音开头讲薯片卖到 6 倍价钱，price 信息被念到，B 项 Ever-rising prices. 借这个原词诱
选；但涨价是“短缺造成的结果”，不是“影响本地产出的因素”，把结果当成因，属答非所
问。
借用原文：being sold for 6 times their normal price
C) 张冠李戴
录音提到 Japanese laws limit、block imports，带有“管制”色彩，C 项 Government
regulation. 借此让人误以为相关；但政府管制说的是“限制进口”这件事，与“影响本地产出”
无关，属张冠李戴。
借用原文：Japanese laws limit the amount of imported potatoes
D) 未提及
录音通篇没提投资，D 项 Diminishing investment. 的 investment 是凭空添加的概念，靠
“农业不景气可能缺投资”这种联想骗人，原文无任何对应。

questions.stem: What does the man think of Mr. Brown's lectures?

explain.定位:
M: Mr. Brown's lectures are so boring.
男：布朗先生的讲座太无聊了。
explain.信号:
本人直接评价句。男士开口第一句 Mr. Brown's lectures are so boring. 就是对讲座的直接
评价，态度题答案信号即说话人本人带感情色彩(so boring)的判断句。
explain.替换:
so boring ↔ Dull.
boring=dull同义替换
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
Informative. 偏向女士那句 the subject is interesting 的褒义气质，但那是女士说『主题有
趣』、且 interesting 也不等于 informative；男士本人是嫌无聊，把女士的褒义安到男士
头上即张冠李戴。
借用原文：the subject is interesting
B) 过度推断
Inspiring.(鼓舞人心)同样取自女士对主题的褒义评价方向 the subject is interesting，且把
『有趣』过度拔高为『鼓舞人心』，既错了人又拔高了程度。
借用原文：the subject is interesting
D) 未提及
Shallow.(肤浅)虽与 Dull. 同为贬义、听着像『也是说不好』，但男士只说讲座 so
boring(无聊)，从没评价内容『肤浅』，无中生有。

questions.stem: What does the woman do during Mr. Brown's lectures?
options: A) She types on a keyboard.

explain.定位:
W: Well, what I do is keep my pen moving.
女：嗯，我做的就是让我的笔一直动着。
explain.信号:
被问者的直接应答。男士问她怎么保持专注，女士直接应答 what I do is keep my pen
moving——对话题答案就落在被问者的回答里，what I do is 更是直接交代『我做的事』
的强信号。
explain.替换:
keep my pen moving ↔ She takes notes.
笔一直动=写=记笔记
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
She types on a keyboard. 盗用了录音原词 keyboard，但原文是 it has to be done by
hand, not typing on a keyboard——明说『要手写、不是在键盘上打字』，选项恰恰取了
被否定的那一项，与原文相反。
借用原文：not typing on a keyboard
B) 未提及
She does recording.(录音)在原文中根本没出现，女士全程谈的是手写与朗读；这是凭『上
课总有人录音』的常识硬塞，无中生有。
C) 原词陷阱
She takes photos.(拍照)易让人联想到后文女士说自己上课会 I draw a little too(还会画点
东西)，但『画画』不是『拍照』，且本题问的是她课上主要做什么(手写)，把 draw 误读成
拍照属答非所问。
借用原文：sometimes I draw a little too

questions.stem: Why does the woman draw in class?
options: A) It keeps her mind active.
B) It makes her stay awake.
C) It enables her to think hard.
D) It helps her kill time.

explain.定位:
It can keep the mind active, prevent getting bored and help to concentrate.
它能让头脑保持活跃、防止厌倦、帮助集中注意力。
explain.信号:
罗列功能的解释句。女士解释画画作用时一口气列出 It can keep the mind active,
prevent getting bored and help to concentrate.——it can 引出的功能罗列句正是 Why
题的答案信号，直接交代『为什么这么做』。
explain.替换:
keep the mind active ↔ It keeps her mind active.
几乎原话照搬人称
explain.排除:
B) 偷换概念
It makes her stay awake.(让她保持清醒)看着像原文 prevent getting bored(防止厌倦)，
但『防厌倦』不等于『不犯困/保持清醒』，把防无聊偷换成防瞌睡，偷换概念。
借用原文：prevent getting bored
C) 过度推断
It enables her to think hard. 借了原文 help to concentrate(帮助集中注意力)的影子，但
『集中注意力』不等于『努力深度思考(think hard)』，把集中拔高成苦思，过度推断。
借用原文：help to concentrate
D) 与原文相反
It helps her kill time.(打发时间)与原文 keep the mind active(让头脑活跃)方向恰好相反
——画画是为了积极投入，不是消磨时间；录音也从未说 kill time，属无中生有且反向。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about reading out loud?
options: A) It enables her to improve her pronunciation.
B) It helps her better remember what she learns.
C) It turns out to be an enjoyable way of learning.
D) It proves to be far more effective than writing.

explain.定位:
If I'm at home and I need to study, what I do is read out loud. It has a similar effect to writing
by hand. It helps memorize information in a physical way.
如果我在家需要学习，我会大声朗读。它的效果与手写类似，能以一种身体参与的方式帮助
记住信息。
explain.信号:
话题词后紧跟的作用陈述。女士说到 read out loud 后紧接着 It helps memorize
information in a physical way.——题干提到的话题词(朗读)出现后，紧随其后的那句作用
陈述就是答案信号。
explain.替换:
It helps memorize information ↔ It helps her better remember what she learns.
memorize=remember同义
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
It enables her to improve her pronunciation.(改进发音)是顺着 read out loud(大声读)想
当然地联想——一听『大声朗读』就觉得是练发音，但女士明说朗读是为了 helps
memorize information(帮助记忆)，从没提发音，答非所问。
借用原文：read out loud
C) 未提及
It turns out to be an enjoyable way of learning.(是一种享受的学习方式)听着像总评、挺
顺耳，但女士只说朗读帮助记忆、效果与手写相似，从没说它『令人享受』，无中生有。
D) 与原文相反
It proves to be far more effective than writing.(比手写有效得多)盗用了原文的比较对象
writing，但女士的原话是 It has a similar effect to writing by hand.——明说『效果相
似』，选项却篡改成『有效得多』，把相似偷换成更强，与原文相反。
借用原文：It has a similar effect to writing by hand.

questions.stem: For what purpose did the woman go to India?
options: B) To try authentic Indian food.
C) To take photos of the Taj Mahal.
D) To trace the origin of a love story.

explain.定位:
We went there about ten years ago for our honeymoon.
我们大约十年前去那儿度蜜月。
explain.信号:
for 引出此行目的。被问者应答里的 for our honeymoon 用介词 for 直接点出去印度的目
的，正是目的题要锁定的缘由句；目的题的答案信号常落在 for/to 引导的目的状语上。
explain.替换:
for our honeymoon ↔ To spend her honeymoon.
同义改写：介词短语换成不定式
explain.排除:

questions.passage:
Food-as-Medicine Movement Is Witnessing Progress

A) Several times a month, you can find a doctor in the aisles of Ralph's market in Huntington Beach, California, wearing a white coat and helping people learn about food. On one recent day, this doctor was Daniel Nadeau, wandering the cereal aisle with Allison Scott, giving her some idea on how to feed kids who persistently avoid anything that is healthy. "Have you thought about trying fresh juices in the morning?" he asks her. "The frozen oranges and apples are a little cheaper, and fruits are really good for the brain. Juices are quick and easy to prepare, you can take the frozen fruit out the night before and have it ready the next morning."

B) Scott is delighted to get food advice from a physician who is program director of the nearby Mary and Dick Allen Diabetes Center, part of the St. Joseph Hoag Health alliance. The center's 'Shop with Your Doc' program sends doctors to the grocery store to meet with any patients who sign up for the service, plus any other shoppers who happen to be around with questions.

C) Nadeau notices the pre-made macaroni(通心粉) and cheese boxes in Scott's shopping cart and suggests she switch to whole grain macaroni and real cheese. "So I'd have to make it?" she asks, her enthusiasm fading at the thought of how long that might take, just to have her kids reject it. "I'm not sure they'd eat it. They just won't eat it."

D) Nadeau says sugar and processed foods are big contributors to the rising diabetes rates among children. "In America, over 50 percent of our food is processed food," Nadeau tells her. "And only 5 percent of our food is plant-based food. I think we should try to reverse that." Scott agrees to try more fruit juices for the kids and to make real macaroni and cheese. Score one point for the doctor, zero for diabetes.

E) Nadeau is part of a small revolution developing across California. The food-as-medicine movement has been around for decades, but it's making progress as physicians and medical institutions make food a formal part of treatment, rather than relying solely on medications(药物). By prescribing nutritional changes or launching programs such as "Shop with your Doc", they are trying to prevent, limit or even reverse disease by changing what patients eat. "There's no question people can take things a long way toward reversing diabetes, reversing high blood pressure, even preventing cancer by food choices," Nadeau says.

F) In the big picture, says Dr. Richard Afable, CEO and president of ST. Joseph Hoag Health, medical institutions across the state are starting to make a philosophical switch to becoming a health organization, not just a health care organization. That feeling echoes the beliefs of the Therapeutic Food Pantry program at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, which completed its pilot phase and is about to expand on an ongoing basis to five clinic sites throughout the city. The program will offer patients several bags of food prescribed for their condition, along with intensive training in how to cook it. "We really want to link food and medicine, and not just give away food," says Dr. Rita Nguyen, the hospital's medical director of Healthy Food Initiatives. "We want people to understand what they're eating, how to prepare it, the role food plays in their lives."

G) In Southern California, Loma Linda University School of Medicine is offering specialized training for its resident physicians in Lifestyle Medicine — that is a formal specialty in using food to treat disease. Research findings increasingly show the power of food to treat or reverse diseases, but that does not mean that diet alone is always the solution, or that every illness can benefit substantially from dietary changes. Nonetheless, physicians say that they look at the collective data and a clear picture emerges: that the salt, sugar, fat and processed foods in the American diet contribute to the nation's high rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. According to the World Health Organization, 80 percent of deaths from heart disease and stroke are caused by high blood pressure, tobacco use, elevated cholesterol and low consumption of fruits and vegetables.

H) "It's a different paradigm(范式) of how to treat disease," says Dr. Brenda Rea, who helps run the family and preventive medicine residency program at Loma Linda University School of Medicine. The lifestyle medicine specialty is designed to train doctors in how to prevent and treat disease, in part, by changing patients' nutritional habits. questions.stem: How could California's drought crisis be solved according to some researchers?
options: A) By building more reserves of groundwater.
B) By drawing water from the depths of the earth.
C) By developing more advanced drilling devices.
D) By upgrading its water distribution system.
questions.passage: California has been facing a drought for many years now, with certain areas even having to pump freshwater hundreds of miles to their distribution system. The problem is growing as the population of the state continues to expand. New research has found deep water reserves under the state which could help solve their drought crisis. Previous drilling of wells could only reach depths of 1,000 feet, but due to new pumping practices, water deeper than this can now be extracted (抽取). The team at Stanford investigated the aquifers(地下蓄水层)below this depth and found that reserves may be triple what was previously thought. It is profitable to drill to depths more than 1,000 feet for oil and gas extraction, but only recently in California has it become profitable to pump water from this depth. The aquifers range from 1,000 to 3,000 feet below the ground, which means that pumping will be expensive and there are other concerns. The biggest concern of pumping out water from this deep in the gradual settling down of the land surface. As the water is pumped out, the vacant space left is compacted by the weight of the earth above. Even though pumping from these depths is expensive, it is still cheaper than desalinating(脱盐)the ocean water in the largely coastal state. Some desalination plants exist where feasible, but they are costly to run and can need constant repairs. Wells are much more reliable sources of freshwater, and California is hoping that these deep wells may be the answer to their severe water shortage. questions.passage:
The AlphaGo program's victory is an example of how smart computers have become.

But can artificial intelligence (AI) machines act ethically, meaning can they be honest and fair?

One example of AI is driverless cars. They are already on California roads, so it is not too soon to ask whether we can program a machine to act ethically. As driverless cars improve, they will save lives. They will make fewer mistakes than human drivers do. Sometimes, however, they will face a choice between lives. Should the cars be programmed to avoid hitting a child running across the road, even if that will put their passengers at risk? What about making a sudden turn to avoid a dog? What if the only risk is damage to the car itself, not to the passengers?

Perhaps there will be lessons to learn from driverless cars, but they are not super-intelligent beings. Teaching ethics to a machine even more intelligent than we are will be the bigger challenge.

About the same time as AlphaGo's triumph, Microsoft's 'chatbot' took a bad turn. The software, named Taylor, was designed to answer messages from people aged 18-24. Taylor was supposed to be able to learn from the messages she received. She was designed to slowly improve her ability to handle conversations, but some people were teaching Taylor racist ideas. When she started saying nice things about Hitler, Microsoft turned her off and deleted her ugliest messages.

AlphaGo's victory and Taylor's defeat happened at about the same time. This should be a warning to us. It is one thing to use AI within a game with clear rules and clear goals. It is something very different to use AI in the real world. The unpredictability of the real world may bring to the surface a troubling software problem.

Eric Schmidt is one of the bosses of Google, which owns AlphaGo. He thinks AI will be positive for humans. He said people will be the winner, whatever the outcome. Advances in AI will make human beings smarter, more able and "just better human beings."

questions.passage:
The AlphaGo program's victory is an example of how smart computers have become.

But can artificial intelligence (AI) machines act ethically, meaning can they be honest and fair?

One example of AI is driverless cars. They are already on California roads, so it is not too soon to ask whether we can program a machine to act ethically. As driverless cars improve, they will save lives. They will make fewer mistakes than human drivers do. Sometimes, however, they will face a choice between lives. Should the cars be programmed to avoid hitting a child running across the road, even if that will put their passengers at risk? What about making a sudden turn to avoid a dog? What if the only risk is damage to the car itself, not to the passengers?

Perhaps there will be lessons to learn from driverless cars, but they are not super-intelligent beings. Teaching ethics to a machine even more intelligent than we are will be the bigger challenge.

About the same time as AlphaGo's triumph, Microsoft's 'chatbot' took a bad turn. The software, named Taylor, was designed to answer messages from people aged 18-24. Taylor was supposed to be able to learn from the messages she received. She was designed to slowly improve her ability to handle conversations, but some people were teaching Taylor racist ideas. When she started saying nice things about Hitler, Microsoft turned her off and deleted her ugliest messages.

AlphaGo's victory and Taylor's defeat happened at about the same time. This should be a warning to us. It is one thing to use AI within a game with clear rules and clear goals. It is something very different to use AI in the real world. The unpredictability of the real world may bring to the surface a troubling software problem.

Eric Schmidt is one of the bosses of Google, which owns AlphaGo. He thinks AI will be positive for humans. He said people will be the winner, whatever the outcome. Advances in AI will make human beings smarter, more able and "just better human beings."

writing.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write a short essay on the challenges of living in a big city. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.model:
Living in a big city may look glamorous, but it actually confronts ordinary residents with a series of tough
challenges. From my point of view, three of them stand out and deserve our serious attention.
To begin with, the high cost of living places a heavy financial burden on city dwellers. Renting even a small
apartment near the centre can easily swallow half of an average monthly salary. In addition, overcrowding
makes daily life exhausting, for commuters are often packed into a crowded subway carriage for more than an
hour twice a day. Moreover, the fast pace and fierce competition leave many people constantly stressed, while
neighbours living next door barely know one another.
In conclusion, expensive housing, overcrowding and mounting pressure are the real prices of urban life. Only
by budgeting wisely and setting aside time to relax can we cope with these challenges instead of being
overwhelmed by them.

translation.directions: Directions: 将下列段落译成英文。
translation.source: 由于通信网络的快速发展，中国智能手机用户数量近年来以惊人速度增长。这极大地改变了许多人的阅读方式。他们现在经常在智能手机上看新闻和文章，而不买传统报刊。大量移动应用程序的开发使人们能用手机读小说和其他形式的文学作品。因此，纸质书籍的销售受到了影响。但调查显示，尽管智能手机阅读市场稳步增长，超半数成年人仍喜欢读纸质书。
translation.reference: Thanks to the rapid development of communication networks, the number of smartphone users in China has grown at an astonishing speed in recent years. This has greatly changed the way many people read. They now often read news and articles on their smartphones instead of buying traditional newspapers and magazines.
